Here’s a general, art-studio-friendly workflow for producing lifelike, display-only replicas of historical banknotes—while keeping them obviously non-negotiable and staying out of legal trouble.

1. Legal & Ethical Ground Rules  
   •   In the U.S., 18 U.S.C. § 504 requires that reproductions of currency be either  
       – one-sided only, or  
       – at least 150 percent or at most 75 percent of the genuine note’s linear dimensions, or  
       – prominently stamped “SPECIMEN,” “COPY” or “FOR DISPLAY ONLY” in lettering at least 16 points high.  
   •   Other countries have similar rules—always check local statutes before you begin.  
   •   Work only from images in the public domain (most pre-1920 currency) or from your own high-res scans.  

2. Materials & Equipment  
   •   Paper: 100% cotton-rag or cotton/linters blend, 80–120 gsm, size adjusted per legal requirements.  
   •   Inks: pigment-based (fade-resistant) for inkjet or laser; plus a spot-color or two if you want metallic/security-style inks.  
   •   Printer: high-res inkjet or laser for fine detail. For a more “authentic” intaglio look you can branch into photo-polymer plate and letterpress or an etching press.  
   •   Foil/embossing tools (optional): small foil-stamp machine or hand-held heated die, plus embossing blankets.  
   •   UV-reactive or iridescent pigment (optional) for a showy “security stripe.”  
   •   Art-grade tea, coffee or very dilute acrylic washes for aging.  

3. Artwork & Prepress  
   a. Source or scan a public-domain note at 600–1 200 dpi.  
   b. Clean up in Photoshop or GIMP—remove background noise, isolate design elements.  
   c. Reconstruct missing bits (corners, edges, seals) using vector tools.  
   d. Lay out your sheet, allowing for bleed and legal “COPY”/“SPECIMEN” overprint.  
   e. If you plan an intaglio effect: separate out the “line work” layer for plating onto a photo-polymer plate.  

4. Printing Techniques  
   •   Digital Print + Hand Finishing (simplest)  
       – Print one side only (legal compliance) on your cotton paper.  
       – For a metallic thread: press a narrow foil stripe into a hot-foil die.  
       – Emboss the central portrait or border with a simple hand-held embosser.  
   •   Two-Pass Hybrid (more realistic)  
       1.   Pass #1: black “intaglio” layer via photo-polymer/letterpress for raised feel.  
       2.   Pass #2: four-color (CMYK) offset or digital print for background tints.  
       3.   Optional Pass #3: spot-color or UV ink for a faux security stripe.  

5. Finishing & Distressing  
   •   Tea/Coffee Wash: lightly brush or mist diluted tea for age staining. Blot immediately to avoid over-soak.  
   •   Creases & Edge Wear: fold and unfold manually, then sand edges gently with ultra-fine sandpaper.  
   •   Small tears: make half-tears, then tear off the rest—torn edges look more authentic than cut ones.  

6. Final Marking & Mounting  
   •   Prominently stamp or overprint “COPY,” “SPECIMEN” or “ART REPLICA” in a contrasting color or with a custom rubber stamp.  
   •   Mount behind UV-filtered plexiglass or frame under museum-grade glass to protect inks and paper.  

7. Checklist Before Display  
   [ ] Size is altered by at least ±25 percent, or one-sided only  
   [ ] “COPY”/“SPECIMEN” clearly visible in ≥ 16 pt type  
   [ ] No attempt to mimic serial numbers in circulation  
   [ ] Inks are non-toxic and light-fast  
   [ ] All local reproduction laws have been reviewed  

By following these steps you’ll end up with museum-worthy replicas that look—and even feel—remarkably like the originals, yet remain unmistakably art objects. Enjoy your project!
